acceptanceCriteria: Both stable consumers give the same verdictSha256 for the converted f0fda542 map, or the spec states the partial drift list is not part of an UNSUPPORTED result and both consumers conform, with a shared vector.
body: Observed 2026-10-12 on branch claude/v1-1275-convert (base b8ef66364) by the V1-1275 parity run (docs/build-log/evidence/v1-1275/parity.jsonl row 558, summary.json). For the 877-hunk map .corvint/changes/f0fda542*.cem.json converted to cem/1.0, native internal/cem/verify/stable.go and interop/cem01-go verify-stable-canonical both give UNSUPPORTED repository unsupported-resource-limit with equal per-hunk arrays, but their partial drift lists differ (native 68 entries, portable 102, the 0.2 source verifier 34) and so their verdictSha256 differ (5341d9b0... vs 92747a60...). Reproduced in two runs. Not caused by the converter; it is a divergence between the two stable consumers on what a resource-limit abort may report. Expected: both consumers either report the same partial drift list or omit it from the digested result on an abort.
title: Stable verifiers diverge on the partial drift list for the f0fda542 resource-limit abort
